 Top questions to ask for open enrollment
 Zach Myers 
 3 hours ago 
 WXIN/WTTV — Before making your health coverage selections during open enrollment this year, experts recommend asking several key questions.
 Open enrollment for the ACA Marketplace starts Nov. 1. If you get health insurance through your employer, your company may have different dates for your open enrollment period.  
 When it’s time for you to decide on your coverage for 2027, Health Markets recommends asking several questions before you finalize your decisions.
 How have my health needs changed?  Do you or someone in your family have a new condition, planned surgery, pregnancy or new medications? Significant life changes can affect how much coverage you need for the year ahead.
 How much healthcare did I really use this year?  Review things like your doctor visits, emergency care, prescription costs and ongoing treatments. If you didn’t need much care, you might want to explore a plan with lower premiums and higher deductibles. If you needed more care, the opposite could be true and you might want to explore a plan with higher premiums and lower deductibles.
 Are my doctors and medicines still covered?  Networks and drug coverages can change from year to year. Make sure you know if your doctor and any specialists are still in network and your prescriptions are still going to be covered.
 What can I afford in premiums and out-of-pocket costs?  Consider all the costs of the coverage like the deductible, copayments and out-of-pocket maximum. Not just the monthly premium.
 If you buy coverage through the Health Insurance Marketplace, the Affordable Care Act offers tax credits for those who meet the income, coverage and residency requirements. In general, your household income must fall between 100% and 400% of the federal poverty level. If you qualify, the tax credits can help lower your monthly premium.
